title: Align Write tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all Write improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go Write covers the basic create/overwrite path, shared ReadState, parent directory creation, atomic write, structured patch generation, team-memory secret rejection, history hooks, optional LSP hooks, and several alignment tests. It is still not TS-exact. The highest-risk gaps are model-visible/structured output shape, strict input and permission semantics, stale-write robustness, post-write ReadState lifecycle, line-ending and encoding policy, symlink/file-mode behavior, un-wired skill/LSP/editor lifecycle hooks, file-history metadata, remote git diff shape, and Go-only notebook/documentation/memory analytics behavior. This report is analysis-only; no tests were run.

task_02

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Go returns model-visible JSON that does not match the TS Write data/result contract
improvement_points.description: TS Write returns structured data with exactly the outputSchema fields `type`, `filePath`, `content`, `structuredPatch`, `originalFile`, and optional `gitDiff`, then maps that data to short model-visible success text. Go serializes an expanded JSON object directly into ToolResult.Content, omits top-level `content`, adds Go-only fields (`isNew`, `bytes`, `lineCount`, `status`, `path`, `diagnostics`, `userModified`, `metadata`, `warning`, `remoteGitDiff`), and therefore changes both API transcript content and programmatic result shape.

improvement_points.title: Go does not enforce TS strict-object input validation or the same path normalization boundary
improvement_points.description: TS uses z.strictObject, describes file_path as absolute, and backfills observable input by expanding `~` and relative paths before hook/permission allowlists see it. Go's shared JSONSchema cannot express additionalProperties:false, parseInputOrError uses json.Unmarshal which ignores unknown keys, and Write trims file_path then resolves with filepath.Abs without shell-style `~` expansion. This permits TS-invalid inputs and changes path identity for whitespace or tilde paths.

improvement_points.title: Write permission decisions are not equivalent to TS checkWritePermissionForTool
improvement_points.description: TS Write delegates to the edit permission system, checks deny rules during validateInput, handles ask/allow/session .claude exceptions, path safety, suggestions, and working-directory decisions. Go Write only enforces AllowedDirs/symlink-safe path containment internally, while the loop has a generic optional PermissionHandler and a separate protected-path SafetyCheck. That does not reproduce TS's per-tool updatedInput, rule source, suggestion, acceptEdits, and deny/ask/allow ordering semantics.

improvement_points.title: Go lacks TS's full-read content fallback for benign mtime changes
improvement_points.description: TS rejects stale writes when mtime moved after the last read, but for full reads it compares current normalized content to the stored read content to avoid false positives from cloud sync, antivirus, or timestamp-only touches. Current Go Write rejects immediately when mtime is newer than the ReadState timestamp, even if the current bytes still match the read snapshot.

improvement_points.title: Post-write ReadState can participate in Go Read dedup where TS prevents it
improvement_points.description: TS Write refreshes readFileState after a successful write so future writes are not stale, but it sets offset and limit to undefined. TS Read dedup requires offset to be defined, so a post-write state entry cannot produce file_unchanged. Go Write stores a ReadFileEntry with zero Offset/Limit and LastTool='Write'; Go Read dedup compares only offset, limit, and mtime, so a subsequent Read can incorrectly dedup against the post-write state entry.

improvement_points.title: Go rewrites model-supplied line endings and preserves extra encodings that TS does not
improvement_points.description: TS Write deliberately stops preserving the old file's line-ending convention and writes the model-supplied content as-is, using the detected file encoding. Go normalizes CRLF and bare CR to LF before writing. Go also detects and re-encodes UTF-16BE, BOM-less UTF-16, Latin-1, and UTF-8 BOM metadata, whereas TS detectEncodingForResolvedPath only returns utf16le for UTF-16LE BOM and otherwise utf8. These choices may be useful, but exact byte output can differ from TS for CRLF payloads and non-TS-detected encodings.

improvement_points.title: Go rejects symlink writes and resets existing file mode instead of matching TS write-through and permission preservation
improvement_points.description: TS's low-level writer detects symlinks, resolves the target, writes through to the target, and preserves the existing target mode on atomic temp replacement. Go refuses to overwrite any symlink target and always calls atomicWriteFile with 0644, so overwriting an executable or custom-mode file can change permissions.

improvement_points.title: Write does not trigger TS skill discovery and conditional skill activation in Go
improvement_points.description: TS Write discovers skill directories for the written path, records dynamicSkillDirTriggers for display, adds skill directories in the background, and activates conditional skills for matching paths. Go has comparable skill discovery machinery for Read, but FileWriteTool has no SkillManager field and SetupRegistry only wires FileReadTool.SkillManager.

improvement_points.title: Go's LSP and editor notifications are optional shims, not the wired TS lifecycle
improvement_points.description: TS Write always calls diagnosticTracker.beforeFileEdited, clears delivered diagnostics for the file, notifies the shared LSP manager with didChange and didSave when available, and calls notifyVscodeFileUpdated with old and new content. Go has optional LSP/DiagnosticsTracker/VSCodeNotifier fields and tests for manually injected fakes, but SetupRegistry wires Write to NewNoopLSPDiagnoser with no DiagnosticsTracker or VSCodeNotifier. The LSPTool's manager is constructed separately and not shared with Write; the VSCode notifier callback receives only new content, so it cannot reproduce the TS diff notification payload.

improvement_points.title: File history tracking differs in timing, gating, and identity metadata
improvement_points.description: TS conditionally tracks file history before the atomic read-modify-write section using updateFileHistoryState and parentMessage.uuid, so backups are correlated with the tool use/message even if later staleness fails. Go appends a JSONL entry after a successful write, ignores failures, generates an EditID when missing, has no visible feature gate, and does not carry the parent message UUID or AppState-style updateFileHistoryState semantics.

improvement_points.title: Remote git diff shape, gating, and analytics differ
improvement_points.description: TS attaches optional `gitDiff` as a structured ToolUseDiff only when both CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE and the `tengu_quartz_lantern` feature are enabled, and logs diff computation analytics. Go uses a package-global SetRemoteGitDiffEnabled toggle, shells out to `git diff`, truncates a string, and places it under `remoteGitDiff`; no SetupRegistry wiring or analytics equivalent is visible.

improvement_points.title: Go adds runtime notebook/documentation/memory behaviors that TS Write does not enforce
improvement_points.description: TS prompt text tells the model to prefer NotebookEdit/Edit and not create documentation unless explicitly requested, but FileWriteTool itself does not reject .ipynb writes or emit a warning field for Markdown creation. TS analytics logs only paths ending in CLAUDE.md. Go rejects .ipynb writes, adds warning to new Markdown/README/CHANGELOG JSON payloads, logs AGENTS.md and local variants through isClaudeMemoryWritePath, and invalidates a Go memory mtime cache. These may be desirable product policies, but they are not exact TS runtime parity.

improvement_points.title: Current Write tests lock several Go-only behaviors and miss key TS parity edges
improvement_points.description: Go has useful tests for core writes, read-before-overwrite, stale rejection, partial read rejection, symlink rejection, payload counts, plan mode, allowed dirs, history, and optional LSP hooks. However, tests currently assert Go-only output fields and policies, contain stale comments claiming older missing fields, and do not cover TS-compatible short tool_result text, top-level content/gitDiff data shape, strict unknown-key rejection, tilde expansion, permission-rule ordering, stale content fallback, post-write Read dedup suppression, CRLF preservation, file mode preservation, default registry LSP/skill wiring, file-history message correlation, or remote diff gating.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Write output data and model-visible tool_result with TS
dependencies: Coordinate with any existing loop/tool-result structured-output work so ToolResult can carry TS-style data without forcing JSON into Content.
WRITE-TASK-011 should supply the final gitDiff shape.
acceptance_criteria: Create returns structured data with type=create, filePath, content, structuredPatch=[], originalFile=null, and optional gitDiff only.
Update returns structured data with type=update, filePath, content, non-empty structuredPatch when content changes, originalFile, and optional gitDiff only.
The model-visible tool_result content matches TS text for create and update.

Go-only fields isNew, bytes, lineCount, status, path, diagnostics, warning, remoteGitDiff, userModified, and metadata are absent from the TS-shaped Write data unless explicitly moved to non-model internal metadata.
implementation_subtasks.notes: This is the largest integration task because current ToolResult is text-first. Keep the compatibility layer narrow and avoid changing unrelated tools unless a shared structured-output carrier is already planned.

implementation_subtasks.title: Make Write input validation strict and path expansion TS-compatible
dependencies: If strict parsing is generalized in parse.go, audit other tools before switching defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Write rejects unknown top-level keys.
Write rejects missing or non-string file_path/content with TS-like validation errors.
Write expands ~ and relative paths consistently before permission, read-state, and filesystem checks.
Write no longer silently changes target identity by trimming leading/trailing file_path whitespace unless TS does the same.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Schema-only additionalProperties is not enough because direct registry execution bypasses provider-side schema validation.

implementation_subtasks.title: Reproduce TS edit permission decision semantics for Write
dependencies: WRITE-TASK-002 should land first so permission checks see TS-expanded paths.
Coordinate with Bash/Edit/NotebookEdit permission parity because TS uses the shared Edit permission namespace.
acceptance_criteria: Edit deny rules block Write before filesystem mutation.
Ask rules and outside-working-directory writes produce TS-equivalent ask decisions and suggestions.
Session-scoped .claude skill allow rules work without permanently allowing broad .claude writes.
acceptEdits mode allows writes in allowed working directories.
Protected paths follow TS ask/suggestion semantics unless a deliberate Go safety override is documented separately.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Do not collapse this into AllowedDirs only; TS permission behavior is richer than path containment.

implementation_subtasks.title: Prevent post-write ReadState entries from satisfying Read file_unchanged dedup

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Write byte output for line endings and encoding
dependencies: WRITE-TASK-004 may need the same normalized-content comparison policy.
acceptance_criteria: A Write content string containing CRLF is written with CRLF bytes, matching TS FileWriteTool behavior.
Bare CR content is not rewritten unless TS does so.
UTF-16LE BOM overwrite behavior matches TS.
UTF-16BE, BOM-less UTF-16, Latin-1, and UTF-8 BOM behavior is either TS-exact or explicitly feature-gated/documented as a non-parity extension with tests.
implementation_subtasks.notes: The TS comments are easy to misread: passing 'LF' stops preserving old CRLF; it does not normalize the model's new content.

implementation_subtasks.title: Match TS symlink write-through and file mode preservation
dependencies: WRITE-TASK-003 should provide resolved-path permission checks before symlink write-through is enabled.

implementation_subtasks.notes: Do not enable write-through without checking both the symlink path and resolved target path, because TS permission code checks both.
